- Import: `import { PopoverTrigger } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: button
- Composition: Child of Popover. Accepts Button props.
- Use when: The button that opens a Popover.
- Avoid:
  - Using it outside Popover.
- Accessibility: A real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | md | Button size of the trigger. |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "accent"` | no | secondary | Button style of the trigger. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

#### Example
```tsx
<PopoverTrigger variant="secondary">Filters</PopoverTrigger>
```

### PopoverContent

The popover panel with its title and description. Place it inside `Popover`.

- Category: overlays
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { PopoverContent } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: div with role dialog in a portal, with a title
- Composition: Child of Popover. Requires `title`; `description`, `side` and `align` are optional.
- Use when: The panel shown by a Popover.
- Avoid:
  - Leaving out the title.
- Accessibility: Labelled by its title. Focus is returned to the trigger on close.

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Heading of the panel. Required: it is the accessible name of the popover. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "start" \| "end"` | no | center | Alignment against the trigger. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | no |  | The content: text, a form, or `PopoverClose` buttons. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Short explanation, announced as the accessible description. |
| `side` | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | no | bottom | Preferred side of the trigger. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

#### Example
```tsx
<PopoverContent title="Filters" description="Narrow the results.">
  <PopoverClose>Done</PopoverClose>
</PopoverContent>
```

### PopoverClose

A button that closes the popover. It is rendered as a `Button`.

- Category: overlays
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { PopoverClose } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: button
- Composition: Inside PopoverContent. Children are the label.
- Use when: A button that closes the Popover.
- Avoid:
  - Icon-only without a label.
- Accessibility: A real button.

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | sm | Button size. |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "accent"` | no | secondary | Button style. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

#### Example
```tsx
<PopoverClose>Done</PopoverClose>
```

## Menu

A dropdown list of actions or links, built on Base UI Menu (arrow keys, typeahead, focus return and
Escape come from there). Items with `href` are real links; items with `onSelect` are actions.
Do not put form controls in a menu: use `Popover`. The trigger icons follow its button size;
menu items are compact and use 16px icons.

- Category: overlays
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { Menu } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: button that opens a role menu with menuitems
- Composition: Pass `label` (the button text) and `items`: `{ label, startIcon?, endIcon?, onSelect?, href?, disabled?, destructive? }` or `{ type: "separator" }`. Icons are generated icons without `size`; the trigger follows its button size and menu items are compact (16px).
- Use when: A list of actions or links behind one button, such as account actions.
- Avoid:
  - Navigation between sections of the site: use links.
  - Form choices: use Select.
- Accessibility: Arrow keys, Home, End, typeahead and Escape come from Base UI. Items with `href` are real links.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `MenuEntry[]` | yes |  | Items in order. Use `{ type: "separator" }` to group them. |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Text of the button that opens the menu. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "start" \| "end"` | no | start | Alignment of the menu against the trigger. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | md | Button size of the trigger. |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "accent"` | no | secondary | Button style of the trigger. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Menu label="Account" items={[
  { label: "Profile", href: "/profile" },
  { type: "separator" },
  { label: "Sign out", onSelect: signOut },
]} />
```

## Accordion

Collapsible sections built on Base UI Accordion. Each title is a button inside an `h3`
(`aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` come from Base UI). Pass `items` instead of composing parts.
The plus/minus sign sits at the end: its vertical stroke collapses while opening.

- Category: navigation
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { Accordion } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: div with a heading (h3) and button per item and a region per panel
- Composition: Pass `items` ({ value, title, content, startIcon?, endIcon?, disabled? }). Icons are generated icons without `size`. Use `multiple` to allow several open, `disabled` to disable every item and `bordered` for a border around the whole list. To place it inside a Card use `Card` + `CardContent`.
- Use when: Showing long content in short sections, such as FAQs.
- Avoid:
  - Hiding content users must read.
  - Navigation between pages.
- Accessibility: Each title is a button in a heading with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `AccordionItem[]` | yes |  | The items, in order. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | no | false | Draw a border and rounded corners around the whole list, not only between items. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | no |  | Ids of the panels open at first. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no | false | Disable every item. A per-item `disabled` still applies on top. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | no | false | Allow several panels open at once. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string[]) => void)` | no |  |  |
| `value` | `string[]` | no |  | Ids of the open panels, when you control it. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Accordion items={[
  { value: "a", title: "Is it accessible?", content: <p>Yes.</p> },
  { value: "b", title: "Is it themeable?", content: <p>Yes.</p> },
]} />
```

## Table

Data table with a real `table`, `caption`, `th scope="col"` and a first-column row header. The wrapper
scrolls horizontally on small screens and is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it.
For layout, use `Grid` or `Stack`, never a table.

- Category: layout
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { Table } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: table with caption, thead, tbody, th scope and a focusable scroll region
- Composition: Pass `caption`, `columns` ({ key, header, align? }) and `rows` (objects by key). Use `align: "end"` for numeric columns: they align end and use tabular numbers.
- Use when: Comparing data across rows and columns.
- Avoid:
  - Page layout: use Grid or Stack.
  - Missing caption.
- Accessibility: Real table semantics. The first column is a row header. The scroll wrapper is focusable and named.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `caption` | `string` | yes |  | Describes the table. Required: it is the accessible name and the visible caption. |
| `columns` | `TableColumn[]` | yes |  | Column definitions, in order. |
| `rows` | `Record<string, ReactNode>[]` | yes |  | One object per row, keyed by `columns[].key`. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `hideCaption` | `boolean` | no | false | Visually hide the caption (it stays available to screen readers). |
| `rowKey` | `string` | no |  | Key of the row value that is unique per row. Falls back to the row index. |

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Table caption="Plans" columns={[{ key: "name", header: "Plan" }, { key: "price", header: "Price", align: "end" }]}
  rows={[{ name: "Free", price: "$0" }, { name: "Pro", price: "$12" }]} />
```

## Breadcrumb

Where the current page sits in the site. Renders `nav > ol` and marks the last item with
`aria-current="page"`. Links use whatever `LinkProvider` provides (`next/link` in this app).

- Category: navigation
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { Breadcrumb } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: nav with an ordered list; the last item has aria-current page
- Composition: Pass `items` ({ label, href?, startIcon?, endIcon? }) from root to current page. `separator` defaults to `>` and accepts any node, such as `/` or `·`; it is always hidden from assistive technology. Use `maxItems` (3 or more) to collapse the middle items into an ellipsis menu opened from an icon button labelled Show hidden pages and sized to its content; omit it to show every item. Icons are generated icons without `size`.
- Use when: Hierarchical navigation: showing where a page sits in a site with 3 or more levels.
- Avoid:
  - Wizards or steps: not a breadcrumb.
  - Using the current page as a link: it is a span with aria-current="page".
- Accessibility: nav > ol; the nav is labelled Breadcrumb by default; the current page is a span with aria-current="page"; separators are hidden from assistive technology; plain links keep keyboard navigation and a visible focus ring.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `BreadcrumbItem[]` | yes |  | The trail from the root to the current page. The last item is marked as the current page. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | no | Breadcrumb | Accessible name of the navigation. Change it when a page has more than one breadcrumb. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `maxItems` | `number` | no |  | How many items to show before collapsing the middle ones into an ellipsis menu. Values below 3 are ignored. Omit it to show every item. |
| `separator` | `ReactNode` | no | > | Node between items. Any node is allowed; it is always hidden from assistive technology. |

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={[{ label: "Docs", href: "/docs" }, { label: "Components", href: "/docs/components" }, { label: "Button" }]} />
<Breadcrumb maxItems={4} items={[{ label: "Docs", href: "/docs" }, { label: "Components", href: "/docs/components" }, { label: "Navigation", href: "/docs/components/navigation" }, { label: "Breadcrumb", href: "/docs/components/breadcrumb" }, { label: "Examples" }]} />
```

## Pagination

Page links for content split across URLs. Every page is a real link, so it works without JavaScript and
with `next/link` through `LinkProvider`. Previous and next are left out (not disabled) when unavailable.

- Category: navigation
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { Pagination } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: nav with a list of links
- Composition: Pass `page`, `pageCount` and `hrefTemplate` such as `/blog?page={page}`.
- Use when: Moving through content split across URLs.
- Avoid:
  - Passing a function for the href (it breaks in Server Components).
  - Infinite lists.
- Accessibility: Every page is a link; the current one has aria-current. Previous and Next are removed, not disabled, when unavailable.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hrefTemplate` | `string` | yes |  | URL of a page, with `{page}` where the number goes, for example `"/blog?page={page}"`. A string (not a function) so it works from Server Components. |
| `page` | `number` | yes |  | Current page, starting at 1. |
| `pageCount` | `number` | yes |  | Total number of pages. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | no | Pagination | Accessible name of the navigation. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Pagination page={2} pageCount={9} hrefTemplate="/blog?page={page}" />
```

## Progress

Progress of a task, built on Base UI Progress (`role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`).
For a quick wait with no known end, prefer `Spinner`; for a value the user sets, use `Slider`.

- Category: feedback
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { Progress } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: div with role progressbar
- Composition: Pass `label` and `value` (number, or null when unknown). Optional `max`.
- Use when: Showing how far a task has got.
- Avoid:
  - Values the user sets: use Slider.
  - Short unknown waits: use Spinner.
- Accessibility: role progressbar with aria-valuenow; the label is the accessible name.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | What is progressing. Required: it is the accessible name. |
| `value` | `number \| null` | yes |  | Current value. Use `null` when the amount is unknown (indeterminate). |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `max` | `number` | no | 100 | Maximum value. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | no | true | Show the percentage next to the label. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Progress label="Uploading" value={40} />
```

## Slider

Pick a number, or a range, by dragging or with arrow keys. Built on Base UI Slider (each thumb is an
`input type="range"`). For a short list of exact choices use `Select`; for typing a number, use `Input`.
Inside `Field` it inherits `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.

- Category: controls
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { Slider } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: div with one input type range per thumb
- Composition: Pass `label` and `defaultValue` (number or [min, max]). Use `thumbLabels` for ranges. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field.
- Use when: Choosing a number or range by dragging.
- Avoid:
  - Exact entry: use Input.
  - A few named options: use Select.
- Accessibility: Each thumb is a native range input with arrow-key support. The label is the accessible name. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; required prints Required; read-only stays focusable and blocks changes; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | What the slider sets. Required: it is the accessible name. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `data-force` | `"focus"` | no |  | Story/test hook: force the focus ring without moving focus. |
| `defaultValue` | `number \| number[]` | no |  | Initial value, or `[min, max]` for a range. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no |  |  |
| `error` | `string` | no |  | Error message. Marks the slider invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`. Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no | false | Shows a small spinner next to the value, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the slider not interactive. |
| `max` | `number` | no |  |  |
| `min` | `number` | no |  |  |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: number \| number[]) => void)` | no |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | no | false | The slider can be focused and read but not changed. Uses the sunken track and keeps the label at full contrast. Distinct from `disabled`. |
| `required` | `boolean` | no | false | The slider must have a value before the form can be submitted. The label prints "Required". Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field instead. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | no | true | Show the current value next to the label. |
| `step` | `number` | no |  |  |
| `thumbLabels` | `string[]` | no |  | Names of the thumbs of a range, for example `["Minimum price", "Maximum price"]`. |
| `value` | `number \| number[]` | no |  | Controlled value, or `[min, max]` for a range. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Slider label="Volume" defaultValue={40} />
<Slider label="Price" defaultValue={[20, 80]} thumbLabels={["Minimum price", "Maximum price"]} />
<Slider label="Budget" error="Choose a budget" required />
```

## Label

A visible label for a form control, in the shared `label` text style.
Prefer `Field`, which also wires the description, error and required state.
Use this when you build a custom composition outside Field.

- Category: controls
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { Label } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: label
- Composition: Text children, `htmlFor`, and optional `required` (prints "Required"; the control still needs its own required attribute) and `disabled`. Prefer Field, which wires description, error and ARIA.
- Use when: A visible label for a custom control composition outside Field.
- Avoid:
  - Replacing Field for a standard form field.
  - Using it as a heading or body text.
  - Relying on an asterisk for required: Label spells out "Required".
- Accessibility: Associate it with the control through `htmlFor`. Required state must also be on the control (native or ARIA).

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Text of the label. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no | false | Dims the label and removes the pointer cursor. Use only when the control is disabled. |
| `htmlFor` | `string` | no |  | The id of the control this label belongs to. |
| `required` | `boolean` | no | false | Prints "Required" after the text. The control still needs its own `required` attribute. |

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<Label htmlFor="name" required>Name</Label>
```

## EmptyState

A quiet placeholder for a region with no content, with an optional icon and action.
The icon is decorative; the title carries the meaning.

- Category: feedback
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { EmptyState } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: section with a heading
- Composition: Pass `title` (required), optional `description`, `icon` (generated icon, no `size`), `action` (usually a Button, with `href` for navigation) and `as` for the heading level (h2-h4, default h3).
- Use when: A region that has no content yet, with a next step.
- Avoid:
  - Errors and failures: use Alert.
  - Loading placeholders: use Skeleton.
  - Decorating a section that already has content.
- Accessibility: The title is a real heading and carries the meaning; the icon is decorative. Keep the heading level in order with the page.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Short title of the empty state. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Main action, usually a Button (with `href` for navigation) or Link. |
| `as` | `"h2" \| "h3" \| "h4"` | no | h3 | Heading level for the title. Keep the page outline in order. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | no |  | One or two sentences that explain what to do next. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Icon above the title. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the component sizes it. |

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<EmptyState
  icon={<FolderIcon />}
  title="No projects yet"
  description="Create a project to start collecting feedback."
  action={<Button>New project</Button>}
/>
```

## Sidebar

A vertical navigation panel for the side of an app layout. Items can be links or buttons;
links use the component from `LinkProvider`. This is a layout piece, not a Base UI primitive.

- Category: navigation
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { Sidebar } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: aside with a nav landmark and a list
- Composition: Pass `label` (required), `items` ({ label, href?, onSelect?, startIcon?, active?, disabled? }), optional `header` and `footer`. Links render with the LinkProvider component; items without href are buttons.
- Use when: Primary vertical navigation beside an app's content, especially on desktop.
- Avoid:
  - Main site navigation in a header: use SiteHeader or links.
  - More than one primary sidebar on a page.
  - Using it for unrelated actions: use Menu or a toolbar.
- Accessibility: The nav landmark is named by `label`; the active item gets aria-current="page". Disabled items are not focusable links and are not clickable.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `SidebarItem[]` | yes |  | The navigation items, in order. |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Required. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Content below the navigation, pinned to the end. |
| `header` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Content above the navigation, such as a title or a workspace switcher. |

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Sidebar
  label="Workspace"
  header={<Heading as="h2" size={6}>Acme</Heading>}
  items={[
    { label: "Overview", href: "/", startIcon: <HouseIcon />, active: true },
    { label: "Settings", href: "/settings", startIcon: <GearIcon /> },
  ]}
/>
```

## Collapsible

One section that expands and collapses, built on Base UI Collapsible. For a set of sections
use `Accordion`; use this for a single disclosure, such as advanced options.

- Category: navigation
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { Collapsible } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: div with a button trigger and a region panel
- Composition: Pass `title`, panel `children`, optional `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`), open state (`defaultOpen`, `open`, `onOpenChange`) and `disabled`.
- Use when: A single section that expands, such as advanced options or extra details.
- Avoid:
  - A set of sections: use Accordion.
  - Hiding critical content users must read.
  - Navigation between pages.
- Accessibility: The trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the panel is its region. Keyboard behavior comes from Base UI.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Panel content. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Visible title. It is the button that opens the panel. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | no | false | Open at first render, when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no | false | Disables the trigger. |
| `endIcon` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Icon after the title, before the chevron. Pass a generated icon without `size`. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` | no |  |  |
| `open` | `boolean` | no |  | Controlled open state. |
| `startIcon` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Icon before the title. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the trigger sizes it. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Collapsible title="Advanced settings">
  <p>Only the options most people need are visible.</p>
</Collapsible>
```

## ToggleGroup

A segmented single-choice control built on Base UI Toggle Group. Use it for two to five short,
mutually exclusive options, such as a view switch. For longer content use Tabs; for independent
on/off choices use Checkbox.

- Category: controls
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { ToggleGroup } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: div role="group" with toggle buttons
- Composition: Pass `label` (required accessible name), `items` ({ value, label, startIcon?, disabled? }), optional controlled value, `size` (sm or md) and `disabled`. Single choice only.
- Use when: Two to five short, mutually exclusive options, such as a view switch.
- Avoid:
  - Long content changes: use Tabs.
  - Independent on/off choices: use Checkbox or Switch.
  - More than five options: use Select.
  - Related actions that are not a choice: use ButtonGroup.
- Accessibility: Arrow keys move between toggles and roles come from Base UI. The group needs its `label`; selected state is exposed with aria-pressed.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `ToggleGroupItem[]` | yes |  | The options, in order. |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name of the group. Required. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | no |  | Initially selected value, when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no | false |  |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | no |  | Called with the selected value, or an empty string when nothing is selected. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | no | md | Control height: `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2.25rem. |
| `value` | `string` | no |  | Selected value, when controlled. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<ToggleGroup
  label="View"
  defaultValue="list"
  items={[
    { value: "list", label: "List" },
    { value: "grid", label: "Grid" },
  ]}
/>
```

## ScrollArea

A styled scroll container built on Base UI Scroll Area. Use it for a fixed-height panel, such as
a list or a code area, where the page itself should not scroll. The viewport is keyboard focusable.

- Category: layout
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { ScrollArea } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: div frame with a focusable scroll viewport and custom scrollbars
- Composition: Pass `children`, optional `label` (accessible name of the scroll region) and `className` to set the height. Default maximum block size is 12rem; override it with a layout class.
- Use when: A fixed-height list, code area or panel that should scroll inside the page.
- Avoid:
  - The whole page scrolling: let the page scroll.
  - Overflowing menus and popups: they handle it themselves.
  - Horizontal-only swipe carousels with no keyboard alternative.
- Accessibility: The viewport is keyboard focusable and shows a focus ring, so keyboard users can scroll it. Give it `label` when the content is not self-explanatory.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The scrollable content. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Class for the outer frame. Use it to set the height. |
| `label` | `string` | no |  | Accessible name of the scrollable region. |
| `viewportClassName` | `string` | no |  | Class for the scrolling viewport. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<ScrollArea label="Activity" className="h-64">
  <Stack gap="3">{items}</Stack>
</ScrollArea>
```

## Sheet

A side sheet for secondary tasks and settings, built on Base UI Drawer. Focus is trapped, Escape
closes it, and it can be swiped away on touch. For a centered decision use `Modal`.

- Category: overlays
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { Sheet } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: a trigger button; when open, a backdrop and a side panel in a portal
- Composition: Pass `trigger` (button text), `title`, optional `description`, `children`, `footer`, `side` (left or right, default right) and open state. One component, no parts.
- Use when: Secondary tasks, settings and filters that slide in from an edge.
- Avoid:
  - A centered decision: use Modal.
  - Non-essential information: use Tooltip or inline content.
  - Sheets without a title.
- Accessibility: Focus is trapped and returned, Escape closes, the page behind is inert, and the title names the sheet. The close button has an accessible label.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Accessible name of the sheet, shown at the top. |
| `trigger` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Text of the trigger button. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Main content. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | no | Close | Accessible name of the close button. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | no | false | Initially open, when uncontrolled. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Optional explanation under the title. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Actions shown at the bottom, usually buttons. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` | no |  |  |
| `open` | `boolean` | no |  | Controlled open state. |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right"` | no | right | Edge the sheet enters from. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Sheet
  trigger="Filters"
  title="Filters"
  description="Narrow the results."
  footer={<Button>Apply</Button>}
>
  <Field label="Status"><Select items={statuses} /></Field>
</Sheet>
```

## Combobox

A searchable single-choice field built on Base UI Combobox (filtering, keyboard navigation,
focus and form value come from there). Pass `items` instead of composing parts.
Inside `Field` it inherits `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.

- Category: controls
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { Combobox } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: input role="combobox" with a filterable listbox popup
- Composition: Pass `items` ({ value, label, description?, startIcon?, disabled? }), a `label` or `aria-label`, and optional `placeholder`, `emptyMessage`, `startIcon`, `size` (sm, md, lg) and open/selection state. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field. Icons are generated icons without `size`.
- Use when: Choosing one option from a long list when typing to filter helps.
- Avoid:
  - Fewer than about seven options: use Select.
  - Several choices: use Checkbox or a multi-select pattern.
  - Free text that is not from the list: use Input.
- Accessibility: Filtering, keyboard navigation and focus come from Base UI. Needs an accessible name from `label`, `aria-label` or Field. The popup is announced with the result count.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `ComboboxOption[]` | yes |  | The options, in order. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | no |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `data-force` | `"focus"` | no |  | Story/test hook: force the focus ring without moving focus. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | no |  | Initially selected value, when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no | false |  |
| `emptyMessage` | `string` | no | No results. | Message shown when the filter has no matches. |
| `id` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `label` | `string` | no |  | Visible label. Provide it, or `aria-label`, or put the Combobox inside `Field`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no | false | Shows a small spinner, marks the field busy and makes it not editable. Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `loading` to the Field instead. |
| `name` | `string` | no |  | Submitted with the form. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | no |  | Called with the selected value, or an empty string when cleared. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | no |  | Placeholder shown when no value is selected. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | no | false |  |
| `required` | `boolean` | no | false |  |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | md | Control height: `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2.25rem, `lg` 2.75rem. |
| `startIcon` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Icon before the input. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the field sizes it. |
| `value` | `string` | no |  | Selected value, when controlled. |

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<Combobox
  label="Assignee"
  placeholder="Search people"
  items={[
    { value: "ada", label: "Ada Lovelace", description: "Engineering" },
    { value: "grace", label: "Grace Hopper", description: "Research" },
  ]}
/>
```

## CodeBlock

Preformatted code with syntax highlighting, an icon-only copy button and optional tabs for
alternatives such as bun, pnpm and npm. Colors come from semantic `--syntax-*` tokens, so light
and dark work without extra code. Unknown languages are shown as plain text.

- Category: typography
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { CodeBlock } from "@/ui/server";`
- Renders: server component that highlights with Shiki, wrapped around a client view with an icon-only copy button, optional tabs and a focusable region
- Composition: Pass `code`, optional `language` and `label`. For alternatives such as package managers pass `tabs` ({ label, code }[]) instead of `code`. Use `highlight={false}` for plain text. Never color code by hand; use CodeBlock.
- Use when: Showing code or commands the user will copy.
- Avoid:
  - Inline code: use Kbd or a code element.
  - Long documents.
- Accessibility: The code region is focusable and named; the copy result is announced via role status.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `code` | `string` | no |  | The code to show, as plain text. Use `tabs` instead when there are alternatives (bun, npm, pnpm). |
| `highlight` | `boolean` | no | true | Highlight known languages on the server. Unknown languages fall back to plain text. |
| `highlightLines` | `number[]` | no | undefined | 1-based line numbers to mark with a 2px left bar and a subtle background. No line numbers are rendered. The same lines apply to every tab. |
| `label` | `string` | no | Code | Accessible name of the scrollable code region. |
| `language` | `string` | no |  | Language name. `bash`, `sh` and `shell` show a small terminal icon instead of the word. |
| `tabs` | `CodeTab[]` | no |  | Alternative versions of the same code, usually one command per package manager. The first tab is selected first. |
| `tone` | `"success" \| "default" \| "brand" \| "danger"` | no | default | Color the frame for the kind of message: default, brand, success or danger. |

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Parts

### CodeBlockView

Presentation half of `CodeBlock`: tabs, copy button and the focusable code region.
The server passes highlighted HTML; without it the code stays plain text.

- Category: typography
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { CodeBlockView } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: client-only presentation of a CodeBlock: tabs, copy button and focusable code region
- Composition: Internal to CodeBlock. Use it only in client components; pass pre-highlighted `html`/`tabHtml` when available, otherwise the code stays plain.
- Use when: Client components that cannot render the server CodeBlock.
- Avoid:
  - Server pages: use CodeBlock, which highlights automatically.
  - Coloring tokens by hand.
- Accessibility: The code region is focusable and named; the copy result is announced via role status.

#### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `code` | `string` | no |  | The code to show, as plain text. Use `tabs` instead when there are alternatives (bun, npm, pnpm). |
| `highlightLines` | `number[]` | no | undefined | 1-based line numbers to mark with a 2px left bar and a subtle background. No line numbers are rendered. The same lines apply to every tab. |
| `html` | `string \| null` | no |  | Highlighted HTML for `code`, produced on the server. |
| `label` | `string` | no | Code | Accessible name of the scrollable code region. |
| `language` | `string` | no |  | Language name. `bash`, `sh` and `shell` show a small terminal icon instead of the word. |
| `tabHtml` | `Record<string, string \| null>` | no |  | Highlighted HTML per tab label, produced on the server. |
| `tabs` | `CodeTab[]` | no |  | Alternative versions of the same code, usually one command per package manager. The first tab is selected first. |
| `tone` | `"success" \| "default" \| "brand" \| "danger"` | no | default | Color the frame for the kind of message: default, brand, success or danger. |

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

## Providers and hooks

## LinkProvider

Wires navigation once for the whole app. In Next.js pass `next/link` so every library link gets
client-side navigation and prefetching, with no `render` prop on each one. Without it links are plain `a` elements.

- Category: utility
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { LinkProvider } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: no element: it provides the link component through context
- Composition: Place once near the app root: `<LinkProvider component={NextLink}>`. Link, Button with href, Menu link items, Breadcrumb and Pagination then render with it.
- Use when: Making every link in the library use `next/link` (or another router link) from a single place.
- Avoid:
  - Passing a `render` prop to individual links.
  - Nesting several providers.
- Accessibility: No effect on semantics; the provided component must render an `a`.

### Props
| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `component` | `LinkComponent` | yes |  | The component every `Link`, `Breadcrumb`, `Pagination` and `Menu` link renders with. Pass `next/link` in a Next.js app. |

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
"use client";
import NextLink from "next/link";
<LinkProvider component={NextLink}>{children}</LinkProvider>
```

## TooltipProvider

Shares the open delay between tooltips. The first tooltip waits `delay` ms; moving to the next
one opens instantly (`data-instant` skips the animation). Put it once near the app root.

- Category: overlays
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { TooltipProvider } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: no element
- Composition: Place once near the app root. Optional. `delay` (default 600) applies only to the first tooltip; the next ones open instantly.
- Use when: Shared open delay across tooltips.
- Avoid:
  - Nesting several providers.
- Accessibility: No effect on semantics.

### Props
_No props of its own._

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

## ToastProvider

Place once near the root of the app (inside `Providers`). It renders the stack of toasts and makes
`useToast` available. Built on Base UI Toast (live-region announcements, F6 to reach the toasts, swipe to
dismiss, pause on hover and focus come from there).

- Category: feedback
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { ToastProvider } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: no visible element until a toast is shown; renders a viewport in a portal
- Composition: Place once near the app root, inside Providers. Then call `useToast()` anywhere below it.
- Use when: Short-lived feedback after an action.
- Avoid:
  - Messages that must stay: use Alert.
  - Several providers.
- Accessibility: Live-region announcements, F6 to reach toasts, pause on hover and focus. The dismiss button is labelled.

### Props
_No props of its own._

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
<ToastProvider>{children}</ToastProvider>
```

## useLinkComponent

The anchor component to render links with: the one from `LinkProvider`, or `a`.

- Category: utility
- Base: Own component
- Import: `import { useLinkComponent } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: hook, renders nothing
- Composition: Only needed when building your own link components that should respect LinkProvider. `const LinkEl = useLinkComponent()` returns the provided link component, or `"a"`.
- Use when: Building your own navigation component that should follow LinkProvider.
- Avoid:
  - Calling it in Server Components: it needs a client component.
- Accessibility: The returned component must render an `a`.

### Props
_No props of its own._

Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

## useToast

Show short-lived feedback after an action (saved, copied, failed). Returns `show` and `close`.
For messages that must stay on the page, use `Alert`.

- Category: feedback
- Base: Built on Base UI (@base-ui/react)
- Import: `import { useToast } from "@/ui";`
- Renders: hook, renders nothing
- Composition: `const { show, close } = useToast(); show({ title, description?, tone?, timeout?, startIcon?, endIcon? })`. Icons are generated icons without `size`.
- Use when: Showing a toast after an action finishes.
- Avoid:
  - Calling it outside ToastProvider.
  - Putting the only copy of important information in a toast.
- Accessibility: The tone is never the only signal: write it in the title.

### Props
_No props of its own._

Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

### Example
```tsx
const { show } = useToast();
show({ title: "Saved", tone: "success" });
```

## Design tokens

- Components and pages use semantic tokens only (--color-page, --color-primary-foreground, --space-4, --text-body-size ...).
- Never use --primitive-* tokens or hardcoded colors, sizes or fonts.
- Light/dark is switched by data-theme="light|dark" on <html>; without it the OS preference applies.
- Text styles are sets of variables named --text-<style>-<size|line|weight|tracking|style|family>.

| Variable | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `--font-family-sans` | fontFamily | `'DM Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif` |
| `--font-family-emphasis` | fontFamily | `'Source Serif 4', ui-serif, Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif` |
| `--font-family-mono` | fontFamily | `'Commit Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace` |
| `--font-weight-regular` | fontWeight | `400` |
| `--font-weight-medium` | fontWeight | `500` |
| `--font-weight-semibold` | fontWeight | `600` |
| `--font-style-body` |  | `normal` |
| `--font-size-10` | dimension | `0.625rem` |
| `--font-size-11` | dimension | `0.6875rem` |
| `--font-size-12` | dimension | `0.75rem` |
| `--font-size-13` | dimension | `0.8125rem` |
| `--font-size-14` | dimension | `0.875rem` |
| `--font-size-15` | dimension | `0.9375rem` |
